title: Slope Length Calculator: True Surface Distance
description: Calculate the true slope length from horizontal run and vertical rise with the Slope Length Calculator — the hypotenuse your map hides. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a one-mile horizontal run climbing 500 feet has a true slope length of 5,303.6 feet — only 23.6 feet longer than the map distance, because gentle slopes barely stretch.
quick_answer: The Slope Length Calculator computes the true distance along a slope from its horizontal run and vertical rise, using Pythagoras: length = √(run² + rise²). Enter the run and rise and read the surface distance — the figure that paving, roofing, fencing and tired legs actually have to cover.

use_cases.title: Fence and pipe runs on grades

body.t: Anything laid along the ground — fence wire, pipe, cable, irrigation line — needs the slope length, with extra for sag and joints the geometry cannot know about.
Piste lengths are quoted along the snow. Convert a run's map footprint and vertical drop into the number the lift company prints.

At a 10% grade the slope length exceeds the run by only 0.5%. At 50% grade the excess is 11.8%, and at 100% (45°) it is 41.4% — the hypotenuse tax stays invisible until slopes get serious, then arrives all at once.

A drive with 40 feet of run and 3 feet of rise needs √(40² + 3²) = 40.11 feet of surface — the extra tenth of a foot will not change the concrete order, but the same maths on a 200-foot hillside lane changes it by whole yards.

faq: Why is slope length always longer than the run?
It is the hypotenuse of the right triangle the slope forms with the horizontal and vertical. A hypotenuse is always the longest side — equal to the run only when the rise is zero.
Do GPS tracks measure slope length?
Good track logs sum 3D segment distances and approximate it; many apps report the flatter 2D length. The difference between two apps' totals for one hike is usually this choice, not an error.
Can I get the angle from the same inputs?
Yes — angle = atan2(rise, run). The Slope & Gradient Calculator returns angle, percent and ratio together from the same two numbers.
What if I only know the angle and the run?
Slope length = run ÷ cos(angle). A 100 m run at 20° gives 106.4 m of slope — the same triangle, entered from another side.
Does this work for a whole winding trail?
Segment by segment, then sum. One rise-and-run pair describes one straight slope; a trail is a chain of them, which is what elevation profiles are for.
How much extra material should I order?
Geometry gives the exact surface length; ordering adds a practical allowance for cuts, overlaps and waste on top. The calculator supplies the honest base number, not the allowance.
Is the vertical rise the elevation difference?
Yes — end elevation minus start elevation for a straight slope. The Elevation Finder supplies either endpoint's height when you only know the places.
